section.title: Introduction
section.para: Numeric extraction adds dates, currency amounts, and quantities to document layers. A dateline supplies the reference date for relative expressions. Currency amounts include a BigDecimal value and an ISO currency code. MoneyConversionAnnotator converts these amounts to a target currency using rates for the document date. NumericPacks provides pipelines for these operations.
The extractors require no model or regular expressions. Results include original-text spans. Quantity extraction scans for currency amounts before measurements to exclude overlapping results.

section.title: Temporal, money, and conversion
Annotator contracts
section.para: MoneyAnnotator, QuantityAnnotator, and TemporalAnnotator accept custom extractors. Each extractor must return a non-null list of non-null mentions, ordered by text position with non-overlapping spans within the original text. The adapters reject invalid results with IllegalArgumentException; they do not sort or remove mentions to repair the result. Adjacent spans and zero-width spans at span boundaries are accepted. An empty result adds an empty output layer.

TemporalAnnotator validates the complete absolute extraction before selecting a reference date, then validates the resolved extraction. With a fixed reference date, it performs and validates one extraction pass. The adapters reject an existing output layer before calling the extractor or conversion provider. Provider exceptions propagate without modification.

MoneyConversionAnnotator requires the source amount layer and, unless a fixed date is configured, the document-date layer. Required layers may be empty. Document-date mode accepts at most one date annotation; fixed-date mode ignores that layer. Input values must have the same spans as their annotations; this is checked before conversion begins. A present conversion result must use the requested currency and retain the source span's offsets and type. Invalid provider results raise IllegalArgumentException. Valid amounts are accepted without additional rounding.

section.title: Exchange rates
section.para: EcbFxRates loads the uncompressed history CSV from the ECB reference-rate downloads. Supply the file or an input stream; OpenNLP does not download or bundle rates. Stream loading does not close the input. ECB rates are published for information, and the ECB discourages their use for transactions. Review the ECB data use terms before distributing data or results.

The UTF-8 CSV starts with Date, followed by unique currency codes of 3 uppercase ASCII letters. Fields are unquoted and dates must be unique. Spaces and tabs around fields are accepted. NUL and other non-whitespace control characters are rejected, including in empty fields and missing-quote markers. Include all columns, using a blank field or N/A for an unavailable quote. One additional empty field at the end of a header or record is accepted. Quotes must be positive; an explicit EUR quote must equal 1. Malformed tables raise IllegalArgumentException; reading and UTF-8 decoding failures raise IOException.

The most recent reference date on or before the requested date is used, up to 7 calendar days earlier. If either currency is unavailable on that date, the result is empty; older quotes are not combined with the selected date. A request before the first reference date or more than 7 days after the last applicable reference date also returns an empty result.

Cross-currency conversion multiplies the amount by the target quote, then divides by the source quote with MathContext.DECIMAL64 (16 significant digits, half-even rounding). Amounts are not rounded to a currency's minor unit. Converting to the source currency preserves the amount and decimal scale, but still requires an available quote on a usable date.

Rates and cross-currency results must fit the BigDecimal scale range at 16-digit precision. Intermediate scale overflow does not prevent a representable result. A result outside this range raises ArithmeticException; it is not returned as a missing quote or rounded to zero. Zero amounts remain convertible when a quote is available.

section.title: Ready-made pipelines
section.para: NumericPacks assembles the annotators for one kind of number: money(), quantity(), temporal(), and fullPipeline(). Money, quantity, and full-pipeline variants accept a Locale to select number notation and currency-symbol defaults from JDK locale data. The temporal annotator runs before DocumentDateAnnotator. To add steps such as currency conversion, use the modifiable list from NumericPacks.annotators() or NumericPacks.annotators(Locale).

Currency and quantity extraction default to LATIN_US. Regional factories with currency extraction require a locale with a currency; quantity(Locale) also accepts language-only locales. Locale selection does not translate month names or relative-date words. Empty input produces the configured layers with no mentions. Currency conversion requires an additional annotator and rates.
This example extends the German pipeline using synthetic rates. The conversion uses the document date and preserves the original amount span.

NumericManualExampleTest tests this listing. Each returned list is independent; editing it does not change a built analyzer. Additional annotators must provide distinct output layers and follow their required input layers. Factory analyzers support concurrent requests. For an extended pipeline, verify concurrent-call support in the added annotators and rate providers.

section.title: Dates in timestamps
section.para: Supported suffixes require T and HH:MM. Seconds, a dot or comma fraction, and Z or a numeric offset are optional. Offsets use +HH:MM or -HH:MM. Fractions apply to the last clock component and may have any number of digits. Lowercase t and z are also accepted. Hour 24 requires zero minutes, seconds, and fraction. Offset hours range from 00 through 23; minutes range from 00 through 59. Second 60 is accepted without checking a leap-second calendar.

Malformed clock fields and incomplete offsets do not produce a date mention or supply a document reference date. Extraction continues with later mentions. For example, 2026-07-14T99:99 has no result. These checks recognize the supported suffix forms; they do not provide general timestamp validation.

section.title: Relative dates
section.para: Week values use the ISO week-based year, which can differ from the calendar year near January 1. Relative counts from 0 to 99 support days, weeks, months, quarters, and years. Reference and resolved dates support the full LocalDate range. If a shift exceeds that range, the expression has no result and extraction continues. Absolute dates written in text remain restricted to years 1000 through 2999.

Normalized years have at least 4 digits. Negative years include a negative sign, as in -0001-01-04; years after 9999 include a positive sign, as in +10000-01-04. Digits and week numbering do not depend on the default locale.

section.title: Document reference date
section.para: DocumentDateAnnotator selects the absolute day mention with the earliest text offset, independent of annotation-list order. Equal start offsets use list order. Relative expressions, months, and coarser values do not supply a date. Without an absolute day mention, the output layer is empty.

section.title: Regional number notations
section.para: The extractors read digits in one written convention, named by NumberNotation: LATIN_US groups with commas and marks the fraction with a dot, LATIN_EU does the opposite. The choice matters: 1.234 is valid in both conventions, but means 1.234 in LATIN_US and 1234 in LATIN_EU. Invalid grouping is rejected. Inputs valid in both are interpreted using the selected notation, without guessing the author's intent.

Both notations read ASCII digits only. Nonbreaking spaces (U+00A0 and U+202F), thin spaces (U+2009), apostrophes (U+0027 and U+2019), and Arabic numeric separators (U+066B and U+066C) between ASCII digits reject an amount rather than produce a partial value. This does not add support for those formats. Ordinary spaces separate tokens and are not interpreted as grouping.
MoneyAmount grouped = new CursorMoneyExtractor(NumberNotation.LATIN_US) .extract("1,234 USD").getFirst(); // amount: 1234 MoneyAmount decimal = new CursorMoneyExtractor(NumberNotation.LATIN_EU) .extract("1,234 USD").getFirst(); // amount: 1.234
List<MoneyAmount> rejected = new CursorMoneyExtractor().extract("$1\u202F234"); // empty: the narrow nonbreaking space is not a supported grouping separator
Scientific notation is not supported: 1e-3kg does not produce a quantity, and $1e-3 does not produce a currency amount. The exponent is not extracted as a separate value.

section.title: Spelled-out currencies
section.para: Currency words use fixed defaults, including dollar for USD, rupee for INR, and pound for GBP. The words peso, franc, krone, and won are not supported. Subunits such as cents and hyphenated compounds such as euro-cent are excluded. Weight phrases such as 3 pounds of flour are interpreted as GBP amounts.

section.title: Quantities
section.para: QuantityAnnotator adds a quantity layer over the raw text, so it requires no other layer. A mention is a number with a percent marker or a unit token; a bare number is never a quantity. Percentages are reported with the unit %, whether written as a sign or as the word percent. No unit conversion is performed: 2.5km keeps the value 2.5 and the unit km.
